svg.text: Forecast-Conditioned Visual Token Allocation and Interleaved Fusion for Time-Series Forecasting

g.title: Per-modality front ends
g.text: out: patched context and per-patch mask
plus (loc, scale), kept for the inverse
each covariate channel becomes its own
token row on the batch axis (mask = 1)
run once offline and cached; tubelets fuse
frame pairs, so 8 frames -> 4 latent slices

g.title: Numeric tokenisation, unchanged from the unimodal checkpoint
g.text: shared by the target row and all 14 covariate rows
The numeric pathway is inherited, not redesigned
Initialised from the unimodal TSFM checkpoint and identical across arms: same backbone, patch
size 16, covariate protocol and schedule. Every behavioural delta belongs to the visual path.

g.title: Resampler-free spatial visual path
g.text: 14 x 14 x 1024 -> 7 x 7 x 1024, 49 cells per slice
per cell: nothing is mixed across spatial cells
learned 49 x 768 table, added by cell index
spatial identity only -- no slice embedding

g.title: Forecast-conditioned token router -- the novel component
g.text: task-conditioned visual relevance scoring: the visual field stays spatially resolved and is never summarised into a global vector
h_TS, pooled from the 42 context tokens
one scalar per (cell, horizon) pair; 2 layers, no cross-cell mixing
196 candidate cells x H horizons -> score matrix

g.title: The same visual field scores differently per horizon
g.text: one visual field, a different relevance map per horizon
A cell is kept because it matters for the target horizon, not because it changed.
Novelty pruning (EVS) is the degenerate case in which f is cosine dissimilarity to the previous slice and ignores both h_TS and e_h.

g.title: Top-K task-relevant visual token selection
g.text: 5. Top-K task-relevant visual token selection (fixed budget)
K = 98 of 196 candidate cells (q = 0.5), global top-k over the router scores
learned top-K routing: soft relevance weights while training, hard top-K at inference

g.title: Interleaved assembly inside the final context patch
g.text: 6. Interleaved sequence assembly -- placement inside context patch 41 (parameter-free)
interleaving is the fusion INTERFACE, not the selection criterion; modality, segment and token-type tags reuse the numeric tables
inside context patch 41 (an 8 h span), before the first future token
each selected cell keeps its spatial address and its slice age
p = 41 + (1 - dt / span) x 0.99, a continuous index in the same coordinate system
K = 98 tokens, ordered by cell address -- not a side branch
The visual tokens sit between the last context token at p = 41 and the first future position at p = 42, not appended after the sequence.
Interleaving is POSITIONAL, not by array order: the encoder is non-causal, so only the rotary index locates a visual token in time.
out: target row [B, 43 + K, 768] = [B, 141, 768] = 42 numeric + 98 visual + 1 future | 14 covariate rows padded to the same length

g.title: Chronos2Encoder
g.text: Chronos2Encoder -- x12 identical blocks (top 3 of 12 train at 0.1x the base learning rate, lower 9 frozen; same policy in every arm)
all 141 tokens: numeric to visual to the
future query, in one attention matrix.
No modality mask, no gate, no cross-
attention side channel, no new kernel.
acts on the BATCH axis: the target row
No visual row here: vision lives inside
the time sequence, never as a sibling
decides WHICH tokens enter, the encoder
h_TS: mean over the 42 context tokens
numeric tokens bypass the router: 42 context + 1 future
last T_hor hidden states, target rows only: [B, 1, 768]
